brief: Transsion-style chamfer × camera matrix with restrained Jali India character
verdict: Reject — one screen violates the evaluation-neutral front contract, and the shared Jali grille was not visibly executed
score_method: All four generated images reviewed and retained. Raw per-image quality is recorded, but a Base Contract failure caps the batch at 59; no output was regenerated or hidden.

visible_evidence: flat rail and symmetric micro-chamfer read clearly
teal/gunmetal/nickel CMF has coherent Transsion-style retail recognition
limitations: bridge extends farther across the back than specified
lower grille resolves as ordinary round perforations rather than the required photo-etched Jali solid–void slot cadence

narrow flat frame and micro-chamfers remain consistent

limitations: backbone approaches a familiar generic vertical pill
Jali process is not visible in the grille

outputs.first_failed_rule: Phone Base Contract 0.1.3 section 4 — Evaluation-neutral front
visible_evidence: broad rear arc and tangent horizontal saddle are visibly different from image 1

outputs.matrix_cell: flat front / broad rear arc × vertical connected axis
visible_evidence: best camera-to-chassis propagation in the batch
planar datum emerges coherently from the broad rear arc
vertical three-lens hierarchy and warm-nickel main ring give strong retail recognition
limitations: the supporting Jali acoustic grille is not rendered as the specified photo-etched two-row slot part

schema_learning: The new camera-to-chassis integration domain successfully makes the 2×2 matrix legible: narrow flat rails produce crisper attached carriers, while broad rear arcs produce supported saddle/datum relationships. However, a repeated neutral-screen rule can still be lost in long prompts, and a small shared cultural carrier can disappear even with departure proof focused elsewhere. v1.5 should keep camera-to-chassis integration, but final consolidation must elevate the neutral-front invariant and distinguish primary departure proof from mandatory secondary-carrier proof.
